title: Container compute
why: Lowest setup effort while reserving six worker vCPU plus headroom.

options.label: One nonburstable EC2 + Compose
advantages: Reuse container tooling; per-service version manifests
At least 8 vCPU supports fair worker caps
disadvantages: Shared host failure/credential boundary
OS, database and backup operations remain team work
options.impact: Recommended; confirm shared-host residual risk, region/SKU and budget.

options.label: ECS Fargate + RDS + managed Redis
advantages: Distinct task IAM roles and task isolation
disadvantages: More IAM/network/release setup
ALB, database, queue and networking cost
options.impact: Keep two logical services, one PostgreSQL server/two DBs and 2-vCPU workers; reprice.

options.label: Inherited non-AWS VM provider
disadvantages: Does not satisfy accepted AD-07 AWS commitment
options.best_when: Only after a recorded proposal amendment
options.impact: Disallowed within current scope; no default fallback.

confirmation: Team must confirm host isolation compromise, account, capacity and budget; a UI click is not authorisation.

title: PostgreSQL hosting
why: Accepted constraint: one PostgreSQL server with two owned databases/roles/migration histories. Self-hosted vs RDS hosting remains a recommended choice.

options.label: PostgreSQL on encrypted EBS
advantages: One server/two DBs fits accepted AD-02
disadvantages: Team patches, backs up and restores
Host outage affects both services
options.impact: Default; enforce roles and retain separate migration histories.

options.label: One RDS PostgreSQL instance, two DBs
disadvantages: Extra cost/network setup
Restore coordination still affects both DBs
options.impact: Preserves AD-02; configure private access and check grants/restore behavior.

confirmation: Confirm host vs RDS and backup owner before cloud bootstrap; two server separation is outside this default.

title: Object storage on AWS
why: Private managed source/output objects avoid another durable server on the demo host.

options.label: Managed S3 source/output stores
disadvantages: Per-service credentials must be scoped
Requests/egress and endpoint parity need verification
options.impact: Recommended; public HTTPS endpoints with private objects and no anonymous listing.

options.label: Self-hosted MinIO on AWS
disadvantages: More storage backup/patch burden
Host-coupled data; browser endpoint TLS work
options.best_when: Only when managed storage cannot fit confirmed constraints
options.impact: Still AWS hosting; source-build recipe and separate MM/worker/cleanup principals required, not root keys.

confirmation: Confirm S3 permissions/lifecycle/cost and restricted credential risk; local MinIO remains the local development plan.

title: Release promotion permission
why: A reviewer checks digest, migrations and triaged reports before automated delivery.

options.label: Manual promotion, automated deploy
disadvantages: Reviewer availability adds wait time
options.impact: After permission, automation runs deploy, health, smoke and rollback; UC-7 starts at first automation after approval/artifact readiness, before OIDC/SSM; gate wait is reported separately.

options.label: Automatic promotion and deploy
disadvantages: Needs established exception/triage rules
Faulty gates may promote unsafe changes
options.best_when: Gates and rollback are already proven
options.impact: Requires team-confirmed policy; mandatory tests and fixable HIGH/CRITICAL gates remain.

confirmation: Confirm reviewers, branch/environment permissions and triage policy; this modal grants no deployment permission.

title: Workload credential delivery
why: Scoped demo keys minimise setup on the planned shared EC2 host; the host-compromise risk remains and has NOT been approved.

options.label: Three scoped demo keys in SecureString
advantages: Small setup effort; works with Compose
Separate MM, worker Put-only and cleanup List/Delete credentials
disadvantages: Long-lived keys need manual rotation/revocation
Host administrators/host compromise can read all mounted secrets; containers are not a hard boundary
options.best_when: Team explicitly accepts the limited demonstration shared-host risk
options.impact: Host role has no S3/workload AssumeRole. Block container IMDS; inject separate permission-limited files outside git/images; mount matching credentials only. Rotate/revoke keys and remove copies at teardown. Current demo risk NOT APPROVED.

options.label: Short-lived STS credentials with refresh broker
advantages: Credentials expire; fewer persistent workload keys
Separate restricted roles preserve the three storage scopes
disadvantages: Broker, refresh scheduling and injection are extra implementation work
Broker/host authority can access all roles; refresh failure can interrupt storage and signing
options.best_when: Team can implement and test refresh lifecycle on Compose
options.impact: Trusted host broker assumes separate workload roles, refreshes before expiry and injects scoped credentials. Containers cannot access broker authority or IMDS. Test expiry, refresh failure, presigned-URL validity and teardown; host compromise remains a risk.

options.label: Separate Fargate task IAM roles
advantages: Managed task credential delivery; no static workload keys
Separate tasks provide stronger workload isolation
disadvantages: More compute/network/release configuration
Managed database/queue/edge and network costs need a new estimate
options.best_when: Credential and workload isolation outweigh minimum setup effort
options.impact: Use separate MM, worker and cleanup task roles with their respective S3 scopes; keep task execution roles separate. No MM and Processing co-location in one task. Confirm the Fargate compute option and budget; two logical services and one PostgreSQL server/two DBs remain.

confirmation: Required before cloud setup: accept the shared-host demo compromise or select a stronger credential plan; name rotation/cleanup owner and confirm budget. A modal click records no approval and provisions nothing.
